result:
New `src/smoother.rs`: `impl LinearKalmanFilter<T> { pub fn smooth(&self, measurements: &[T]) -> KalmanResult<SmoothedEstimates<T>> }` (flat m-per-step slice) and `SmoothedEstimates<T>` (`len`, `is_empty`, `state_dim`, `state(k)`, `covariance(k)`, `states()`, `covariances()`; per-step accessors return Option). `src/filter.rs` gains one re-export inside `pub mod linear`; `src/lib.rs` declares `mod smoother;` plus doc lines; `src/builder.rs` widens `zeros` to `pub(crate)`; DESIGN_NOTES.md records the module and a measured weakness. Tests: `tests/rts_smoother.rs` (6) and `tests/rts_smoother_oracle.rs` (3).
Algorithm: forward pass on a clone calling the filter's own predict/update (no predict before the first measurement, one before every later one), recording filtered x/P and predicted P; backward pass with Gᵀ = (P⁻)⁻¹ F P by Cholesky solve (no inversion), x⁺ = x + G(x⁺ − Fx), P⁺ = P + G D Gᵀ with D = P⁺ − P⁻ ≤ 0, hence trace(P⁺) ≤ trace(P). Output buffers reused in place; the filter is never mutated; same finiteness/PSD post-conditions as `commit`.
Easy: the `pub(crate)` F/Q accessors and `Clone` let the smoother re-run the filter's own steps instead of a second implementation, and the private kernels and the checked `builder::zeros` dropped straight into the backward pass.
Hard: the filter keeps no history, so each step stores two n×n covariances and the predicted mean is recomputed as F·x (same rows and dot order, so bit-identical); smoothing clones and allocates, so B12 covers only predict/update.
Verified: frozen 32, lib 119, new 6 + 3, doctests 12, full `cargo test` green; 1-D random walk within 1e-9 of an independent textbook RTS, trace never increases on 200 steps of four f64 models, 300 random f32 + 300 random f64 models with zero failures.
Known limits: the backward gain needs P⁻ numerically positive definite, which the filter never needs, so f32 SPEC models A and B return SingularMatrix/FilterDivergence rather than an uncertified covariance (f64 passes); the trace rule is proved and tested, not enforced; step convention documented in three places.
